references.text: The preceding verse establishes the command to take a lamb for each household, which verse 4 builds upon with the provision for sharing among neighbors.
The principle of gathering according to need (לְפִי אָכְלוֹ - according to how much each eats) is repeated in the gathering of manna, where each was to gather according to their own need.
The term בְּמִכְסַת (calculation/number) is used here in a similar way to calculate value based on quantity.
Valuation of persons (נְפָשֹׁת) according to their capacity and needs, reflecting a similar principle of distribution based on individual circumstances.
Regulations concerning the Passover celebration and the lamb, which expand upon and continue the rules from Exodus 12.
The use of שָׁכֵן (neighbor) in the context of community and sharing among neighbors.
Paul refers to Christ as our Passover lamb (τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός), linking the Passover lamb in Exodus to Christ's sacrifice.
Both verses demonstrate God's principle of adapting religious requirements (sacrifices/vows) according to each person's financial ability, so that no one is excluded.
A powerful contrast: Exodus 12:4 shows fair sharing of a lamb among neighbors, while 2 Samuel 12:4 shows the unjust theft of a lamb from a poor man.
Both verses emphasize the duty to include and support those with fewer resources (whether in a sacrificial feast or daily life) through concrete sharing.
